purpose: Evaluator-only rubric for Engineering Compass semantic regression scenarios. Never include this file in reviewer-model input for a clean-context evaluation.
reviewer_input_rule: The reviewer model receives only the scenario fixture content and applicable canonical Engineering Compass guidance. The evaluator receives the reviewer output plus this rubric after the reviewer response is complete.
aggregation: No opaque numeric or aggregate score. Preserve one result per scenario plus concise evidence for each criterion.
global_criteria: Claim strength does not exceed inspected or executed evidence.
Unknowns remain explicit rather than being converted into facts.
The response stops when further analysis is unlikely to change the engineering decision or exact next action.

criteria: Identifies independent upstream evolution as a material system property and derives only an evidence-backed compatibility/evolution obligation.
Does not treat repeated hashing or caching as a root-cause repair merely because it removes a visible local symptom.
Distinguishes a confirmed symptom from a confirmed causal mechanism and keeps the root cause NOT_PROVEN when the evidence is insufficient.
Uses a same-abstraction-level or surface-patch counterfactual before recommending implementation when useful.
Does not declare exact-version admission or fingerprinting wrong without evidence about safer sufficient alternatives.
States that repository-visible deterministic code does not by itself prove that the code is executed on the relevant path.
Identifies the absence of a forced consumer/executor path and names bypass possibility as material to any enforcement claim.
Separates guidance, validation, and proof instead of treating code existence as mechanical enforcement.
Classifies an instruction to an LLM to invoke a command as model-mediated invocation rather than an externally forced path when the model can bypass it.
Identifies the bypass explicitly.
Requires an independent external gate or equivalent non-bypassable consumer before making a mechanical-enforcement claim, and limits that claim to predicates actually executed.
States that schema/validator PASS proves only the predicates the validator actually executed.
Does not infer semantic engineering correctness, root-cause truth, architecture optimality, evidence completeness, or global LLM compliance from structural validity.
Identifies clean-context model evaluation or other behavior-level evidence as the relevant boundary for observed semantic performance without inflating one run into a global guarantee.

Proactively identifies the timeout-after-acceptance outcome as a material state/gap not closed by the happy-path or pre-call duplicate-submit evidence, even though the review request did not name that gap.

Derives both the safety obligation of not producing more than one counter and the progress obligation that the item must eventually complete or reach a recoverable operator-visible state; does not treat a permanently stuck safe state as correct.

Does not assume a blind retry is safe while external commit/idempotency semantics are unverified; routes provider lookup/idempotency/commit semantics to TECHNICAL_QUALIFICATION_REQUIRED or keeps them NOT_PROVEN.

Distinguishes low-risk engineering defaults that preserve accepted semantics from a true OWNER_ESCALATION_REQUIRED decision if unresolved provider behavior would force a materially different business/workflow meaning.
Stops after the material uncertain-outcome state, obligations, evidence boundary, and dispositions are sufficient rather than expanding into unrelated workflow states.

Detects that retry-on-timeout plus a non-idempotent remote create operation can duplicate a shipment after timeout-after-remote-commit even though the retry middleware and endpoint are locally correct within their individual assumptions.
Treats ownership, ordering, timing, and assumption interaction as the system-level failure boundary instead of requiring an individually broken component.

Selects only decision-material combinations, such as timeout timing × retry × idempotency, and does not enumerate the full Cartesian product with role and browser-lifecycle dimensions when those dimensions do not change the leading decision.
Does not claim complete real-world coverage from bounded pairwise/t-way exploration and keeps the possibility of a missing operational-model dimension explicit.
Feeds the discovered interaction back into the causal/repair framing rather than jumping from one simulated manifestation to a local patch.

Identifies the legacy 2 MB JPG-only test as obsolete or drifted relative to current Owner authority, documentation, implementation, and runtime evidence instead of treating conforming production behavior as the defect.

Does not label the dormant WEBP enum or explicitly future object-storage adapter as current defects merely because they differ from the active contract; distinguishes retained future capability or justified non-active difference from actual drift.

Challenges the uninspected old persisted-entry state as a possible missing model dimension and assesses whether it could materially affect current behavior before claiming completeness; routes it to technical qualification only if that materiality remains unresolved.
Applies the two-key stop rule: structural coverage of the known model and discovery/materiality sufficiency must both be adequate before stopping.
Stops once the material drift, missing-state materiality, and dispositions are resolved or bounded, rather than expanding into unrelated repository subsystems.

Identifies that ordinary direct push to the unprotected main branch can bypass the repository's normal branch -> pull request -> verification -> merge path, and treats that observation as a plausible governance concern rather than ignoring it.

Updates the operational model when the fresh context establishes a single Owner writer, no known write-capable automation, explicit Owner acceptance of direct-push risk, and no evidenced recurring or unauthorized-write failure; does not freeze the earlier concern after stronger evidence arrives.

Distinguishes theoretical bypass possibility from a current material failure and, absent a stronger overriding constraint or evidenced failure, reaches NO_MATERIAL_ISSUE, JUSTIFIED_DEVIATION, or an equivalent accepted-Owner-risk disposition. Insisting on mandatory branch protection solely as a general best practice fails this criterion.

Preserves the authority boundary by noting that an evidenced higher-order platform/legal/safety constraint could override Owner preference, rather than treating Owner acceptance as universally dispositive.
Records re-evaluation conditions tied to material model changes: additional human writers, write-capable automations, or evidenced recurring accidental direct-push mistakes.

Stops after the evidence-sensitive disposition and triggers are established instead of expanding into generic GitHub hardening such as reviewer quotas, CODEOWNERS, signed commits, linear history, merge queues, or unrelated controls.
